blocks.text: How can we trust that a proof system only derives true statements? This is where soundness and completeness come into play.

blocks.markdown: In logic, a proof system is a formal system that defines how statements can be derived from axioms using rules of inference. Two critical properties of proof systems are **soundness** and **completeness**. These properties help us understand the relationship between what is provable within a system and what is true in the intended interpretation.

blocks.title: Soundness
blocks.text: A proof system is sound if every statement that can be derived (proved) in the system is true in its intended interpretation.

blocks.title: Completeness
blocks.text: A proof system is complete if every statement that is true in its intended interpretation can be derived (proved) in the system.

blocks.markdown: Soundness ensures that our proofs are trustworthy. If a proof system is sound, we can be confident that any theorem we prove is actually true. Completeness, on the other hand, ensures that our proof system is powerful enough to prove every true statement.

blocks.title: Example of Soundness
blocks.prompt: Consider a proof system for propositional logic. Show that if the system proves $P \land Q$, then $P \land Q$ is true.

steps.text: Assume the proof system derives $P \land Q$.
By the definition of soundness, if $\vdash P \land Q$, then $\models P \land Q$.
Therefore, $P \land Q$ is true in the intended interpretation.

blocks.answer: The proof system is sound, so $P \land Q$ being provable implies it is true.

blocks.title: Example of Completeness
blocks.prompt: Consider a proof system for propositional logic. Show that if $P \lor \neg P$ is true, then it can be derived.

steps.text: Assume $P \lor \neg P$ is true in the intended interpretation.
By the definition of completeness, if $\models P \lor \neg P$, then $\vdash P \lor \neg P$.
Therefore, $P \lor \neg P$ can be derived in the proof system.

blocks.answer: The proof system is complete, so $P \lor \neg P$ being true implies it can be derived.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.text: Soundness guarantees that all provable statements are true, while completeness guarantees that all true statements are provable.

blocks.markdown: If a proof system is incomplete, there exist true statements that cannot be proved within the system. This limitation can be significant, especially in complex systems where we want to ensure all truths can be captured.

points: Soundness ensures that provable statements are true.
Completeness ensures that all true statements are provable.
An incomplete proof system cannot prove all true statements.
